coverage_definitions.A_AzurePolicy: Directly enforceable today by one or more Azure built-in policy definitions. Definition names, GUIDs and effects are on the control row.
coverage_definitions.B_AzureConfig: Azure Policy or Entra configuration covers a substantial part of the control, but full coverage needs configuration outside Azure Policy (for example Entra Conditional Access, which has no Azure Policy equivalent).
coverage_definitions.D_MicrosoftAttestation: Microsoft's responsibility under the shared responsibility model. Not customer-configurable. The Azure Policy column names the attesting standard clause and the exact route to the evidence document.
coverage_definitions.C_Process: A process, contractual or organisational control. No Azure Policy can assert it. Evidence is held in the Customer GRC.

controls.description: The senior leadership of the cloud consumer shall mandate the establishment of a cloud security program with apparent oversight and direction and assign resources (budget, people, and technology) for the successful implementation of the program.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Executive mandate, budget allocation and programme sponsorship are organisational acts. No Azure resource property expresses senior-leadership direction, so no Azure Policy can evaluate it. Evidence is a board-approved cloud security programme charter held in the Customer GRC.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall establish and document policies governing critical aspects of cloud security and a process to identify and ensure compliance with the cloud service's applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Authoring and approving written policy is a documentation process. Azure Policy evaluates resource state, not the existence of a corporate policy document. Evidence is the approved policy set and legal/regulatory compliance register.

controls.description: A robust and continuous risk management program shall be established and implemented to include the cloud environment. The program shall be designed to assess, monitor, and mitigate risks throughout the lifecycle of cloud services.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Establishing a continuous risk management programme is a governance process. Microsoft Defender for Cloud can supply risk telemetry as an input, but the programme itself is not an Azure resource configuration and cannot be asserted by policy.

controls.description: Security and privacy risk assessments shall be conducted to analyze the impact on data and assets hosted within the cloud environment. Consumers shall ensure that data classification is properly applied, and that the risk assessment is aligned with the classification of the data, ensuring appropriate protection measures are in place.
controls.how_to_meet: Risk assessment and data classification are analytical activities performed before deployment by the Customer. Microsoft Purview can be used for data classification labelling using Microsoft Purview Information Protection function. Tags can also be used to identify the data classification processed or stored by the resource and security controls can be aplied based on tags.
controls.reason: Risk assessment and data classification are analytical activities performed before deployment. Classification labelling is a Microsoft Purview Information Protection function, not Azure Policy; no built-in evaluates whether an assessment was performed.

controls.description: Effective internal and external risk communication and consultation shall be undertaken at all stages of risk assessment. Senior leadership shall be responsible for acknowledging and formally accepting any identified risks before making decisions to move data and operations to the cloud, ensuring that risks are fully understood and managed at the executive level.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Risk communication, consultation and formal executive risk acceptance are human decision records. There is no Azure resource state to evaluate.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall follow security requirements stated in the UAE Information Assurance Standard for all personnel (employees, vendors and contractors) supporting cloud services.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Personnel security under the UAE Information Assurance Standard covers screening, vetting and HR process for the Customer staff and contractors. This is outside the Azure control plane entirely.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure contractual clauses with CSP's include (i) background screening of CSP personnel, (ii) clearly defined roles, and responsibilities matrix with segregation of duties in a shared responsibility model, (iii) regular user awareness and training program, (iv) a disciplinary process, and (v) orderly exit process, including contract termination.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts.
controls.reason: Contractual clauses binding the CSP (screening, RACI, training, disciplinary, exit) are legal instruments. Enforced through the Microsoft Customer Agreement and Product Terms, not Azure Policy.

controls.control_name: 2.1.4 Third Party and Supply Chain Security
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall be aware of the information shared with or accessible by the CSP's third party suppliers and their supply chain.
controls.how_to_meet: Awareness of information shared with CSP sub-processors is satisfied by reviewing the Microsoft subprocessor list.
controls.reason: Awareness of information shared with CSP sub-processors is satisfied by reviewing the Microsoft subprocessor list. No Azure resource attribute represents this awareness.

controls.control_name: 2.1.4 Third Party and Supply Chain Security
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall identify the security risks of using supply chain resources.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Supply chain risk identification is an assessment activity over third parties, not over Azure resources. No built-in policy definition has this scope.

controls.control_name: 2.1.4 Third Party and Supply Chain Security
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall liaise with the CSP to understand third party suppliers' compliance with the cloud security requirements.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts.
controls.reason: Verifying CSP third-party compliance is done via Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager and the Service Trust Portal attestation library, which are not Azure Policy surfaces.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall engage a third party with adequate skills to conduct independent security control implementation testing.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Engaging an independent third party to test control implementation is a procurement and audit activity. Azure Policy can evidence the resulting findings but cannot assert the engagement.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall seek assurance regarding the security of service design and components by validating the existence of independent third- party testing and assessments performed by the cloud service provider, in lieu of conducting direct in-depth testing.
controls.how_to_meet: ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 9.2 (internal audit) and clause 9.3 (management review); SOC 2 Type II - independent service auditor's opinion Independent third-party testing is evidenced by the annual ISO/IEC 27001 surveillance audit and the SOC 2 Type II report, both performed by an accredited external auditor. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate + Statement of Applicability Where: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC How: Service Trust Portal > Certifications & Regulations > ISO/IEC. Download 'Azure ISO/IEC 27001 Certificate' and the SoA. No NDA required. SOC 2 Type II report (Security, Availability, Confidentiality) Where: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC How: Service Trust Portal > Audit Reports > SOC. Requires sign-in with a work account and acceptance of the Microsoft NDA before download. Azure penetration testing rules of engagement Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/pen-testing How: Customers may run their own penetration tests against their tenancy without prior Microsoft approval, within the published rules of engagement.
controls.reason: Satisfied by Microsoft third-party assurance reports (ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, SOC 1/2/3, CSA STAR) obtained from the Microsoft Service Trust Portal. This is a Microsoft attestation obligation, not a customer-configurable Azure control.

controls.description: Cloud consumer shall perform legal due diligence and review all contractual obligations in detail prior to engaging any cloud services and/or CSP to ensure that the use of any cloud services and/or CSP will be commensurate with the organization's risk profile.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts.
controls.reason: Pre-engagement legal due diligence on the CSP is a legal workstream executed before any Azure resource exists.

controls.description: As part of the contractual agreements, a non-disclosure agreement shall be drafted and formalized, and signed by both parties before cloud computing services are procured.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts.
controls.reason: Execution of a non-disclosure agreement is a contractual act with no Azure resource representation.

controls.description: As part of the contractual agreements, a Service Level Agreement detailing availability, quality of services provided, and actions in the case of a network outage, data loss, or security breach, etc. shall be drafted and formalized, and signed by both parties before cloud computing services are procured.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts and SLAs documented at https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/docs/view/Service-Level-Agreements-SLA-for-Online-Services?lang=1&msockid=207f5ac1bae96a45016d4fb2bbce6bb5
controls.reason: Service level agreement negotiation and acceptance is contractual. Microsoft SLA terms are published in the Service Level Agreements for Microsoft Online Services document.

controls.description: The cloud consumer shall ensure that cloud service contracts include: (a) clear provisions enabling data and service portability, minimizing vendor lock-in (b) defined processes for contract termination and data retrieval, (c) dispute resolution mechanisms that is strictly limited to UAE governing law.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts. Microsoft services that store the Customer data allow the Customer to retrieve this data in a self-service manner.
controls.reason: Portability and UAE governing-law clauses are contract text. Azure Policy cannot evaluate contractual language.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure that contractual agreements with cloud service providers include clearly defined rights to audit the provider's controls, processes, and facilities.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts.
controls.reason: A right-to-audit clause is a contractual entitlement. Microsoft satisfies the underlying assurance need through third-party audit reports rather than customer on-site audit.

controls.description: Policies and procedures shall be established and implemented for data classification, labelling and handling throughout its lifecycle to secure the data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within the service's geographically distributed (physical and virtual) applications, infrastructure, network and systems components and shared with other third parties to ascertain any regulatory, statutory, or supply chain agreement (SLA) compliance impact.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Authoring a data classification and handling policy is a documentation process. The technical enforcement of labels is delivered by Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels, which are not governed by Azure Policy definitions.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall classify their data before migrating to the cloud, based on the potential impact of its compromise on operations, reputation, financial stability, and regulatory compliance and align this classification with the levels outlined in Appendix 6.7 Data Classification Levels.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation. Microsoft Purview can be used for data classification labelling using Microsoft Purview Information Protection function. Tags can also be used to identify the data classification processed or stored by the resource and security controls can be aplied based on tags.
controls.reason: Classifying data before migration is a pre-deployment analysis activity. No Azure Policy built-in can assert that classification was completed prior to migration.

controls.description: Policies and procedures shall be established and implemented, for the use of encryption protocols for the protection of sensitive data at rest (may include but not limited to: file servers, databases, and end-user devices), data in use (memory), and data in transmission (may include but not limited to: system interfaces, over public networks, and electronic messaging) as per applicable legal, statutory, and regulatory compliance obligations.
controls.how_to_meet: Azure Policies to enforce encryption at rest: Azure Recovery Services vaults should use CMK for backup data;Azure Container Instance container group should use CMK;AKS OS and data disks should be encrypted by CMK;HPC Cache accounts should use CMK for encryption;Managed disks should be double encrypted (PMK + CMK);MySQL servers should use CMK to encrypt data at rest;OS and data disks should be encrypted with a CMK;PostgreSQL servers should use CMK to encrypt data at rest;Queue Storage should use CMK for encryption;SQL managed instances should use CMK to encrypt data at rest;SQL servers should use CMK to encrypt data at rest;Storage account encryption scopes should use CMK;Storage accounts should use CMK for encryption;Table Storage should use CMK for encryption Azure Policies to enforce encryption in use: Confidential Computing:Allowed resource types Encryption in Transit: Azure services are accessible over SSL/TLS endpoints
controls.reason: Encryption at rest for the primary data services is directly evaluable. Transparent Data Encryption covers Azure SQL at rest; secure transfer and the minimum TLS version policy cover data in transit for storage. Together these give measurable evidence of the encryption policy being applied to Azure-hosted data.
defender_recommendations: Transparent Data Encryption on SQL databases should be enabled
Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled

controls.description: Keys shall be maintained by the cloud consumer or trusted key management provider. Key management and key usage shall be separate duties.
controls.how_to_meet: Azure Key Vault use RBAC permission model configured by the Customer. the Customer can also make usage of External Key Management (EKM) where the Customer generate, store, and manage encryption keys outside of cloud infrastructure, while using those keys to protect data in cloud services.
controls.reason: Separation of duties over key material is enforced by moving Key Vault off vault access policies onto Azure RBAC, and by preventing irreversible key loss. These built-ins evaluate the vault configuration that makes SoD possible; the assignment of the roles themselves is an Entra ID operation outside Azure Policy.
defender_recommendations: Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled

controls.description: Consumers shall conduct a risk assessment to determine whether Hold Your Own Key (HYOK) capabilities are required to be implemented.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer assessment and Microsoft supports HYOK via External Key Management (EKM)
controls.reason: A risk assessment of the Hold Your Own Key model is an analytical deliverable. Azure Policy can verify the resulting HYOK implementation (see 2.3.2.4) but not the assessment itself.

controls.description: If the risk assessment indicates that HYOK is necessary, consumers shall implement it to retain exclusive control over encryption keys and mitigate the risk of unauthorized access to data.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer assessment and Microsoft supports HYOK via External Key Management (EKM)
controls.reason: HYOK implementation is directly observable: compute disks and the storage and database services holding Confidential/Restricted data must be encrypted with a customer-managed key rather than a platform-managed key. These built-ins evaluate the customer-managed key property on the resource.

controls.description: In cases where HYOK is implemented, consumers shall ensure that key access, revocation, and auditability are supported without dependency on the CSP.
controls.how_to_meet: This is supported by Azure External Key Management (EKM)
controls.reason: Auditability of key access without CSP dependency is met by forcing Key Vault resource logs into a customer-owned Log Analytics workspace or storage account, so the key access trail is held by the Customer rather than only by Microsoft. The built-in evaluates the diagnostic setting; the destination residency is enforced separately by the custom observability-residency definition in the SLZ plane.

controls.description: Location of data shall be known at all stages and handled as per applicable laws, regulations, standards, and frameworks published within the UAE pertaining to data location and sovereignty.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer controls the location of its data in the cloud including Microsoft Policy "Allowed locations"
controls.reason: Data location visibility is achieved by constraining and then auditing where resources may exist. The location allow-list makes the permitted geography explicit and the resource-group location audit surfaces resources deployed outside the intended region.

controls.description: During the selection of cloud service providers, cloud consumers shall ensure that they operate within acceptable legal jurisdiction(s).
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft has two regions in the UAE and via the Allowed locations policy the Customer can ensure your cloud resources are only created within UAE regions.
controls.reason: Verifying CSP jurisdictional compliance is a legal assessment of Microsoft's operating entity and applicable law. Not expressible as Azure resource state.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall verify whether any agreements with the cloud service provider relating to the use of their data by the service provider are acceptable to them and not contrary to relevant local legislation.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts.
controls.reason: Confirming the terms of the data use agreement is a contractual review of the Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure that data classified as Confidential/Restricted* are stored and processed in a Partial Sovereign Cloud or Sovereign Cloud environment.
controls.how_to_meet: The group of policies and configurations described on the other answers will enable the Customer environment to be a Sovereign Cloud environment. For additional security, the Customer can enable the policy "Allowed resource types" that enforces the usage of Confidential Computing for subscriptions processing its most sensitive data.
controls.reason: Residency for Confidential/Restricted data is enforced at deploy time by denying any resource or resource group outside the approved UAE regions. This is the single strongest technical control for residency and is evaluated on every ARM deployment before the resource is created.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure that data classified above Confidential/Restricted* are strictly stored and processed in Sovereign Cloud environment.
controls.how_to_meet: The group of policies and configurations described on the other answers will enable the Customer environment to be a Sovereign Cloud environment. For additional security, the Customer can enable the policy "Allowed resource types" that enforces the usage of Confidential Computing for subscriptions processing its most sensitive data.
controls.reason: Secret/Top-Secret residency uses the same deploy-time location denial, scoped to the sovereign management group archetype only. Note that commercial Azure alone may not satisfy the full sovereign tier; the policy enforces the geography boundary but the sovereignty tier remains subject to blocker B2 (exclusive UAE jurisdiction).

controls.description: Cloud consumers planning to, or using, multiple cloud services shall perform a comprehensive assessment on their needs and requirements for interoperability of their services and respective CSPs.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer architecture guidance needs to ensure interoperability between CSPs. Microsoft services expose well defined APIs and store data in open format facilitating interoperability. Adoption of Managed Services (PaaS) based on open source solutions available in Azure further facilitate interoperability.
controls.reason: Assessing multi-cloud interoperability is a design and architecture study, not an Azure resource configuration.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure that industry standards and available APIs are consistently utilized and applied across their data and cloud services to support interoperability.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer architecture guidance needs to ensure interoperability between CSPs. Microsoft services expose well defined APIs and store data in open format facilitating interoperability. Adoption of Managed Services (PaaS) based on open source solutions available in Azure further facilitate interoperability.
controls.reason: Adoption of open standards is a design decision expressed in solution architecture. No Azure Policy built-in evaluates standards conformance of an application.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall document appropriate policies and procedures defining the requirements for interoperability and clearly communicate it to all parties.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Documenting the interoperability policy is a documentation deliverable.

controls.description: Contractual agreements shall include provisions specifying the cloud consumer's access to all structured and unstructured data in an industry- standard format upon contract termination.
controls.how_to_meet: Covered by the Customer and Microsoft contacts; and Microsoft services enable the Customer to extract its data in a self-service manner. Data stored in Microsoft services utilize industry- standard formats.
controls.reason: Contractual data portability on termination is a contract clause; Microsoft commits to data retrieval periods in the Product Terms.

controls.description: Cloud consumers, when procuring cloud services, shall ensure the CSP has demonstrated its commitment to portability (may include but not limited to, upon contract termination, the length of time for which data will be stored, the controls implemented by CSP for protection of such data and data deletion process) .
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft services expose well defined APIs and store data in open format facilitating portability. Adoption of Managed Services (PaaS) based on open source solutions such as Kubernetes and PostgreDBs, available in Azure, further facilitate interoperability.
controls.reason: The CSP portability commitment is a contractual undertaking by Microsoft.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall document appropriate policies and procedures defining the requirements for portability and clearly communicate it to all parties.
controls.how_to_meet: the Customer Process / organisational implementation.
controls.reason: Documenting portability procedures is a documentation deliverable.

controls.description: Cloud consumers, when procuring cloud services, shall ensure the CSP has adequate change management controls in place such that the status, location and configuration of service components are tracked throughout their lifetime within the service.
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft has a well established change management process which is audited indepedently as part of SOC 2 compliance report. the Customer has access to the SOC 2 report.
controls.reason: Verifying the CSP's own change management controls is an assurance review of Microsoft's SOC 2 report. Azure Policy governs the customer's resources, not Microsoft's internal change process.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall be made available the results of a change or move of an image and the subsequent validation of the image's integrity through electronic methods.
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft provides mechanisms that enable customers to track, validate, and verify the integrity of virtual machine images, backups, snapshots, and other cloud artifacts throughout their lifecycle. Customers can leverage audit logs, activity logs, change tracking, integrity validation mechanisms, and deployment records to monitor image creation, movement, restoration, and modification activities and maintain evidence of integrity verification.
controls.reason: Shared Responsibility. Microsoft provides audit and validation capabilities; Customers are responsible for defining, reviewing, and retaining evidence of image integrity validation.
defender_recommendations: Secure Boot should be enabled on supported Windows virtual machines
Linux virtual machines should use Secure Boot

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall validate the effectiveness of the physical security controls at the CSP data centres before hosting data or procuring any services (the level of security controls applied should take into consideration the classification of data to be hosted).
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft-attested control ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 7 (Physical controls) - 7.1 physical security perimeters, 7.2 physical entry, 7.3 securing offices, 7.4 physical security monitoring; SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria CC6.4 (physical access) Azure datacentre physical security documentation Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/physical-security How: Public Microsoft Learn article describing perimeter, access approval, two-factor building access and asset-destruction process.
controls.reason: Physical and environmental security of Azure datacentres is wholly a Microsoft responsibility under the shared responsibility model. Validation is by ISO/IEC 27001 certificate and SOC 2 Type II report from the Service Trust Portal; customers have no policy surface over it.

controls.description: Policies shall be developed and implemented to ensure all cloud assets and endpoints are catalogued, tracked, and managed securely based on organizational business risk.
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft provides capabilities such as Azure Resource Graph, Azure Policy, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Intune, Azure Arc, and asset discovery and inventory reporting to support asset visibility, governance, and lifecycle management across cloud environments.
controls.reason: Customer Responsibility with Microsoft-supported asset discovery, inventory, and governance capabilities.
defender_recommendations: Microsoft Defender for servers should be enabled

controls.description: Policies and procedures shall be developed and implemented to establish security as a key focus across the application/software development lifecycle such as SecDevOps/DevSecOps.
controls.reason: A secure development lifecycle is a process control executed in the CI/CD toolchain (GitHub Advanced Security, Defender for DevOps). Azure Policy does not evaluate source repositories or pipelines.

controls.description: Cloud consumers, when procuring cloud services, shall ensure that the CSP has adequate application security controls in place.
controls.how_to_meet: No Azure Policy - Microsoft-attested control ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 8.25 (secure development lifecycle), 8.26 (application security requirements), 8.28 (secure coding), 8.29 (security testing in development); SOC 2 CC8.1 (change management) Application security of the platform is attested through the ISO/IEC 27001 Statement of Applicability and the SOC 2 change-management criteria. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate + Statement of Applicability Where: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC How: Service Trust Portal > Certifications & Regulations > ISO/IEC. Download 'Azure ISO/IEC 27001 Certificate' and the SoA. No NDA required. SOC 2 Type II report (Security, Availability, Confidentiality) Where: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC How: Service Trust Portal > Audit Reports > SOC. Requires sign-in with a work account and acceptance of the Microsoft NDA before download.
controls.reason: Verification of the CSP's own application security controls is satisfied by Microsoft SDL attestation and SOC 2 reporting, not by customer-assignable Azure Policy.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure adequate hardening guidelines are developed and implemented for all cloud systems (physical and virtual), including but not limited to operating systems, virtual machines, hypervisors, Internet of Things sensors and network and security devices.
controls.how_to_meet: The definition, implementation, and ongoing maintenance of hardening standards for customer-managed resources are the responsibility of the Customer. Microsoft is responsible for hardening and securing the underlying cloud infrastructure within the scope of the shared responsibility model, while Customers are responsible for applying and monitoring hardening controls on workloads, operating systems, applications, and other resources they deploy and manage.
controls.reason: System hardening is measured in-guest. The Guest Configuration extension is the prerequisite that enables OS baseline evaluation, and the update policy evidences that security patches are applied. Note that the older 'Vulnerabilities in security configuration on your machines should be remediated' definition no longer exists as a single built-in; the live equivalents are named per-OS in Defender.
defender_recommendations: Vulnerabilities in security configuration on your Windows machines should be remediated (powered by Guest Configuration)
Vulnerabilities in security configuration on your Linux machines should be remediated (powered by Guest Configuration)
System updates should be installed on your machines (powered by Azure Update Manager)

controls.description: User authentication environment and ability to manage identities shall be restricted to authorized consumer staff.
controls.how_to_meet: Blocked accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be removed ; Guest accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be removed ; Guest accounts with write permissions on Azure resources should be removed
controls.reason: Restricting identity administration to authorised staff is enforced in Microsoft Entra ID. What Azure Policy can evaluate is the resulting Azure RBAC surface: that no blocked or external guest identity retains permissions on Azure resources.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall implement centralized processes for privileged account (root accounts) creation and strictly control & limit the activities that can be performed through the account.
controls.how_to_meet: A maximum of 3 owners should be designated for your subscription ; There should be more than one owner assigned to your subscription
controls.reason: Centralisation and control of privileged accounts is measured by bounding the number of subscription owners and requiring more than one owner to avoid a single point of administrative failure.
defender_recommendations: A maximum of 3 owners should be designated for subscriptions
There should be more than one owner assigned to subscriptions

controls.description: Multi-factor authentication should be considered for all accounts within the cloud.
controls.how_to_meet: Azure/Entra configuration control
controls.reason: NOT MAPPABLE TO AZURE POLICY. Multi-factor authentication for Azure resource identities is enforced by Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which is not an Azure Resource Manager resource and therefore has no Azure Policy definition. The former Defender for Cloud MFA recommendations ('Accounts with read permissions on Azure resources should be MFA enabled' and siblings) have been retired and no longer exist in live assessment metadata; only AWS and GCP MFA assessments remain. Evidence must be a Conditional Access policy export.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall establish processes and procedures for authenticating access to systems, applications, and data assets by integrating authentication on the cloud with an internal directory service.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer establishes and maintains authentication policies and procedures that integrate cloud services with an approved enterprise identity directory. Microsoft Entra ID supports integration with on-premises and third-party directory services, enabling centralized identity management, single sign-on (SSO), access governance, conditional access, and authentication controls across cloud applications, systems, and data resources.
controls.reason: Federated authentication with directory integration is configured in Microsoft Entra ID. The Azure-side evidence is the elimination of non-federated local credentials: denying storage shared key access and requiring Entra-only client authentication where the service supports it.

controls.description: Role Based Access Controls (RBAC) shall be implemented within management interfaces.
controls.how_to_meet: Audit usage of custom RBAC roles by customer
controls.reason: Role-based access control in management interfaces is evidenced by auditing custom RBAC role definitions, which are the primary route by which least-privilege is broken in Azure.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall implement processes and procedures to verify authorized access to data and system functions.
controls.how_to_meet: Customer can enable audit usage of custom RBAC roles
controls.reason: Verification of authorised access is measured by auditing custom RBAC roles and by confirming no guest identity holds read, write or owner permissions on Azure resources.

controls.description: Multi-factor authentication shall be implemented for accounts with elevated privileges within the cloud.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer can enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all privileged and administrative accounts within the cloud environment. Microsoft provides MFA, Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), and Identity Protection capabilities through Microsoft Entra ID to help secure privileged access and reduce the risk of unauthorized use of elevated accounts.
controls.reason: NOT DIRECTLY MAPPABLE TO AZURE POLICY. Multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts is enforced by Microsoft Entra Conditional Access and Privileged Identity Management, which are Entra ID objects and have no Azure Policy definition. The former Defender for Cloud recommendation 'Accounts with owner permissions on Azure resources should be MFA enabled' has been retired and is absent from live assessment metadata; only AWS and GCP MFA assessments remain. The compensating Azure-evaluable controls bound and clean the privileged population.
defender_recommendations: A maximum of 3 owners should be designated for subscriptions

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall define and implement formal requests and approvals as part of the user access provisioning process.
controls.reason: The formal joiner access provisioning workflow is an identity governance process. Microsoft Entra ID Governance entitlement management delivers it; it is not an Azure Policy surface.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall ensure timely de-provisioning or modification of access of movers/leavers or system identity changes.
controls.how_to_meet: Access approval, entitlement ownership, periodic review frequency, segregation of duties, and recertification decisions are Customer governance responsibilities. Microsoft provides tools to automate and support access reviews; however, the Customer remains responsible for validating that access remains appropriate and aligned with business and regulatory requirements.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall periodically review and recertify access rights and entitlements.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer establishes and operates a formal access review and recertification process for user accounts, privileged roles, service accounts, group memberships, and application entitlements. Access rights should be reviewed at defined intervals and adjusted or revoked where no longer required. Microsoft provides capabilities such as Microsoft Entra ID Access Reviews, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), Identity Governance, auditing, and reporting to support periodic recertification activities.
controls.reason: Periodic access review and recertification is executed by Microsoft Entra ID Governance access reviews, which has no Azure Policy definition. The Azure-evaluable residue of a failed review is stale guest and blocked-account permissions, which these built-ins detect.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall establish incident management processes for the cloud services, which shall be regularly tested and enacted in response to security incidents.
controls.reason: Defining the cloud incident management process is a documentation and organisational deliverable.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Incident management shall include pre-defined processes for responding to common types of incidents and attacks on the cloud environment.
controls.reason: Authoring pre-defined incident response runbooks is a documentation deliverable; the runbooks may automate Azure actions but their existence is not policy-evaluable.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: A defined process and contact route shall be implemented for reporting security incidents.
controls.how_to_meet: Subscriptions should have a contact email address for security issues ; Email notification for high severity alerts should be enabled
controls.reason: The reporting process itself is procedural, but the Azure prerequisite for it to function is a reachable security contact and active alert notification on every subscription. These built-ins evaluate that prerequisite.
defender_recommendations: Subscriptions should have a contact email address for security issues
Email notification for high severity alerts should be enabled

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall be responsible for notifying relevant external entities within acceptable timeframe.
controls.reason: Notifying regulators and national authorities is an external communication obligation. Azure Policy cannot evaluate whether a regulatory notification was sent.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities shall be maintained and regularly updated.
controls.reason: Maintaining a regulatory contact directory is a records-management activity.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall set up clear procedures to activate security incident management, establish the incident response plan in line with the Cyber Security Incident Response Plan issued by the CSC and define a relevant protocol to appraise the management on the development of the incident, containment, and communication to appropriate entities.
controls.reason: Aligning IR activation procedures to UAE Cyber Security Council requirements is a process alignment exercise.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall conduct regular incident simulations to stress-test security incident response plans.
controls.reason: Running incident response simulation exercises is an operational activity with no Azure resource state.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall identify suitable personnel to oversee the setup and ongoing supervision of e-Discovery/Cloud Forensic capabilities with clear and measurable metrics.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer designates appropriately qualified personnel to establish, manage, and oversee e-Discovery and cloud forensic capabilities. Roles, responsibilities, authority levels, and accountability should be formally defined, and measurable performance indicators should be established to monitor the effectiveness of e-Discovery, evidence preservation, forensic investigations, and compliance activities. Microsoft provides eDiscovery, audit, logging, investigation, and compliance capabilities that support Customer-operated forensic and legal discovery processes.
controls.reason: Oversight of e-discovery personnel and capability is an organisational capability control.

controls.domain: 2.8 Security Incident Management, e-Discovery, and Cloud Forensics
controls.description: Cloud consumers shall establish e-forensic protocols coherent with the UAE law enforcement procedures in digital evidence handling and ensure that CSP comply with such protocols.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer establishes and maintains digital forensics and electronic evidence handling procedures aligned with applicable UAE legal, regulatory, and law enforcement requirements. These procedures should address evidence identification, collection, preservation, chain of custody, access controls, retention, and disclosure requirements. Microsoft provides audit logging, monitoring, investigation, eDiscovery, compliance, and data export capabilities that can support customer forensic investigations and evidence preservation activities.
controls.reason: The definition of forensic processes, evidentiary standards, chain-of-custody requirements, interaction with law enforcement authorities, and legal admissibility requirements are the responsibility of the Customer and are jurisdiction-specific. Microsoft provides supporting capabilities and cooperates in accordance with contractual commitments and applicable laws, but the Customer remains responsible for establishing e-forensic protocols and ensuring they meet UAE legal and regulatory requirements.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall establish the requirements for regular backups of information within the cloud environments and the backup restoration testing schedule.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer defines and documents backup requirements for cloud-hosted information, including backup frequency, retention periods, recovery requirements, and restoration testing schedules based on business, operational, and regulatory needs. Microsoft provides backup, recovery, redundancy, and data protection capabilities that the Customer can configure to support these requirements.
controls.reason: Backup coverage is directly evaluable per virtual machine. Restoration testing remains a process obligation, so this control is only partially enforceable: the policy proves backup exists, not that a restore was rehearsed.

controls.description: Cloud consumers shall establish strong encryption requirements for backups while ensuring that restoration efforts are successful for such data.
controls.how_to_meet: Azure Recovery Services vaults should use customer-managed keys for encrypting backup data
controls.reason: Backup encryption with customer-managed keys is an explicit property of the Recovery Services vault and is evaluated by this built-in.

controls.description: Requirements for operational continuity, including uptime, redundancy, high availability and recovery priorities, shall be communicated as part of cloud service contracts, and tested for cloud services.
controls.how_to_meet: Operational continuity requirements, including availability targets, redundancy architecture, resiliency options, service recovery capabilities, and service commitments, are communicated through Microsoft contractual documentation, service descriptions, service level agreements (SLAs), and service-specific documentation. Customers can design workloads to meet their required uptime, high availability, and recovery objectives using Microsoft-provided resiliency features such as Availability Zones, geo-replication, backup, and disaster recovery services. Customers should validate that their deployed architecture meets organizational continuity requirements through regular testing and exercises.
controls.reason: Operational continuity provisions in the cloud contract are contractual text.

controls.description: Business continuity and disaster recovery plans shall be formalized and communicated to all relevant parties (including but not limited to third parties).
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer develops, documents, approves, maintains, and communicates Business Continuity (BC) and Disaster Recovery (DR) plans to all relevant internal and external stakeholders, including employees, service providers, technology partners, and other third parties that have roles in recovery activities. Plans should be periodically reviewed, updated, and exercised to ensure ongoing effectiveness. Microsoft provides service documentation, service continuity information, and recovery capabilities that support the Customer's BC/DR planning and operational resilience requirements.
controls.reason: Formalising and communicating the BC/DR plan is a documentation and awareness activity.

controls.description: Recovery plans shall at a minimum define Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD), Recovery Time Objective (RTO), Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and roles and responsibilities of all relevant parties.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer develops, maintains, and tests business continuity and disaster recovery plans that define: Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD) Recovery Time Objective (RTO) Recovery Point Objective (RPO) Roles, responsibilities, escalation paths, and decision authorities for all relevant stakeholders Microsoft Azure provides resilient infrastructure, availability options, backup, replication, and disaster recovery services (e.g., Azure Site Recovery, Backup, Availability Zones) that customers can use to design solutions aligned to their defined recovery objectives.
controls.reason: Defining MTPD, RTO, RPO and the supporting RACI is a planning deliverable. Azure Policy can enforce the technical configuration that supports the target (see 2.9.1.1 and 3.9.1.1) but cannot assert the objectives themselves.

controls.description: A security governance framework shall be established to ensure procedure, personnel, and physical and technical controls remain effective through the lifetime of the service, in response to changes in the service, changes in threat and technology development.
controls.reason: Microsoft operates a documented, enterprise-wide security governance programme under the Microsoft Security Policy (MSP) and the Microsoft Policy Framework. Azure records its control implementations in the Azure Control Framework and its Standard Operating Procedures. Effectiveness is independently audited annually. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (ISMS clauses 4-10, plus the Statement of Applicability); SOC 2 Type II common criteria CC1-CC5. Microsoft control references IS-1, IS-2, IS-3, PL-2. EVIDENCE: 1. Microsoft Service Assurance - Governance, risk and compliance: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-governance 2. Azure ISO/IEC 27001 certificate and Statement of Applicability - Service Trust Portal > Certifications & Regulations > ISO/IEC: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC 3. SOC 2 Type II report - Service Trust Portal > Audit Reports (NDA required): https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC

controls.description: Security and privacy risks impacting consumer services provided by CSP's shall be continuously monitored and reported on in alignment with a formally documented risk management process.
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft Defender CSPM should be enabled
controls.reason: Continuous security and privacy risk monitoring is delivered by the Defender Cloud Security Posture Management plan, which is the component that produces the risk and attack-path telemetry. The built-in evaluates whether that plan is enabled on the subscription.
defender_recommendations: Microsoft Defender CSPM should be enabled

controls.description: Personnel with access to Consumer Data and systems shall be subject to security screening and background verification checks.
controls.reason: Microsoft screens all candidates before employment, covering education and employment verification. Personnel who maintain Microsoft online services must additionally pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check before being granted access to online-services systems. Evidence is retained in the employee database and the check must be renewed at least every two years; access eligibility is revoked automatically if it lapses. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 6.1 (screening); SOC 2 Type II criterion CC1.4. Microsoft control reference SOC2-12 (Background checks). NOTE: this attests background screening only. It does NOT attest UAE national security clearance, which NCSP 3.1.3.4 additionally requires and which no Microsoft certification covers. EVIDENCE: 1. Microsoft Service Assurance - Personnel security: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-human-resources 2. Azure ISO/IEC 27001 certificate: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC 3. SOC 2 Type II report (NDA required): https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC

controls.description: The CSP shall implement and maintain a comprehensive cloud security training program to ensure all relevant staff are regularly trained on cloud security principles, best practices, and emerging threats.
controls.reason: All Microsoft employees complete foundational security and privacy awareness training on joining, with mandatory annual refresher training thereafter and additional role-based training before specific access is granted. Training is refreshed when system or policy changes warrant it. Standards of Business Conduct training is also mandatory and annually refreshed. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 6.3 (information security awareness, education and training); SOC 2 Type II criterion CC1.4. Microsoft control reference IS-4 (Security training). EVIDENCE: 1. Microsoft Service Assurance - Personnel security and training: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-human-resources 2. Azure ISO/IEC 27001 certificate and Statement of Applicability: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC 3. SOC 2 Type II report (NDA required): https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC

controls.description: A formal exit process for CSP personnel shall be followed as per contractual obligations with cloud consumers.
controls.reason: Microsoft applies defined policies and procedures to revoke physical and logical access promptly when employment ends. Termination status propagates to the account management tool, which automatically removes the domain account, and physical badges and authenticators are collected at exit. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 6.5 (responsibilities after termination or change of employment); SOC 2 Type II criterion CC6.2. Microsoft control reference OA-3 (Account revocation). controls.description: CSP shall provide flexibility to cloud consumers for conducting independent assurance testing of services and components, or alternatively, the CSP may provide a recent and relevant third-party assurance report (e.g. SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, or equivalent) to demonstrate compliance and control effectiveness.

Both routes are available: Azure permits customer penetration testing of its own tenancy under published rules, and the SOC 2 Type II report serves as the third-party alternative. Azure penetration testing rules of engagement Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/pen-testing How: Customers may run their own penetration tests against their tenancy without prior Microsoft approval, within the published rules of engagement. Download 'Azure ISO/IEC 27001 Certificate' and the SoA. No NDA required.
controls.reason: Flexibility for independent assurance testing is satisfied through Microsoft's third-party audit programme rather than customer-led penetration of the platform.

controls.description: CSP contract shall be subjected to legal review to ensure that terms and conditions consider cloud consumer specific security requirements.

No ISO or SOC attestation can confirm that a contract was legally reviewed against the Customer's specific requirements; that review is an the Customer legal activity performed against Microsoft's published terms. Microsoft's terms are published and reviewable in full before signature. the Customer evidence is its own legal sign-off record referencing the executed agreement version. EVIDENCE: 1. Microsoft Product Terms: https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/docs/view/Product-Terms 2. Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum: https://aka.ms/dpa 3. the Customer legal review record for the executed Microsoft agreement (held by the Customer)

Microsoft's confidentiality and non-disclosure practices are nonetheless audited. Microsoft does not expose supplier-level SLAs to customers; the customer-facing commitment is the Azure SLA, under which Microsoft remains accountable regardless of sub-processor performance. controls.description: Policies and procedures shall be developed for the classification, protection, and handling of data throughout its lifecycle, in line with all applicable laws in the UAE and regulations, standards, and risk levels.
controls.how_to_meet: The Customer establishes and maintains data governance, information classification, retention, protection, and handling policies aligned with applicable UAE legal, regulatory, and business requirements. Microsoft cloud services provide supporting capabilities including: Sensitivity labels and data classification Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Information Protection and encryption Retention and Records Management Audit logging and monitoring Access control and identity governance These capabilities enable the Customer to implement and enforce lifecycle management controls for data creation, storage, use, sharing, retention, and disposal.Customer to define, implement, and enforce its own data governance and compliance policies based on business, regulatory, and risk-based requirements.
controls.reason: Microsoft provides the technology platform and compliance capabilities that support data governance and protection requirements. Responsibility for defining data classification schemes, determining data handling requirements, mapping regulatory obligations, and enforcing organizational policies remains with the Customer under the shared responsibility model.

controls.description: CSP shall ensure that access to Consumer Data occurs only with the explicit documented permission of the consumer, and that such access strictly aligns with the consumer's stated preferences and consent requirements.
controls.how_to_meet: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/reports/government-requests/customer-data
controls.reason: Access to consumer data only with explicit permission is operationally delivered by Microsoft Customer Lockbox. Customer Lockbox has no Azure Policy definition, so the policy-evaluable component is limited to auditing custom RBAC roles that could grant broad data access.

controls.description: When a CSP receives a valid and binding order ("Request") from any governmental body ("Requesting Party") for disclosure of consumer data, the CSP shall use every reasonable effort to redirect the Requesting Party to the consumer. Additionally, the CSP shall make every reasonable and lawful effort to inform the consumer & UAE authorities and challenge/ deny the Request. If the CSP remains compelled to disclose consumer data to a Requesting Party, the CSP should disclose only the minimum amount of consumer data necessary to satisfy the Request.
controls.reason: Microsoft publishes a standing commitment to challenge government requests for customer data where there is a lawful basis to do so, to redirect requests to the customer wherever legally permitted, and to notify the customer unless prohibited by law. Microsoft reports the volume and outcome of such requests, including rejections and challenges, twice yearly. ATTESTED BY: not a certification item - this is a published corporate and contractual commitment, evidenced by the transparency reporting record. EVIDENCE: 1. Microsoft Law Enforcement Requests Report (biannual, includes rejected and challenged requests): https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/law-enforcement-requests-report 2. Microsoft 'Defending Your Data' commitment: https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2020/11/19/defending-your-data-edpb-gdpr/ 3. Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum, disclosure of processed data provisions: https://aka.ms/dpa RESIDUAL: 'every reasonable effort' is met, but Microsoft cannot guarantee refusal of a valid US legal order. See the sovereignty gap on 3.3.1.5-3.3.1.7.

controls.description: CSP shall maintain records of all foreign access requests (for a minimum of 10 years), including details on the nature of the request, actions taken, and any communication with national authorities; and make these available to relevant UAE authorities upon request.
controls.how_to_meet: Microsoft makes the Lawfull access report available. https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/reports/government-requests/customer-data

controls.description: All data stored or processed on the cloud service shall remain under the exclusive jurisdiction of the UAE and its competent authorities. The UAE's sovereign rights, legal obligations, and regulatory frameworks governing data ownership and jurisdiction shall be strictly upheld.
controls.how_to_meet: No Azure Policy - Microsoft-attested control ATTESTED BY: NOT ATTESTABLE by ISO/SOC - jurisdictional, requires contractual and legal treatment. No certification attests exclusive UAE jurisdiction. Microsoft is subject to US law including the CLOUD Act. Partial technical mitigation is available and should be combined with contractual commitments. Managed HSM external key management (preview) Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/external-key-management-overview How: Key encryption key stays in a customer-operated HSM outside Microsoft infrastructure. Gated: requires Microsoft account team enablement and USD 10M+ annual committed Azure spend. Azure Confidential Computing Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/overview How: Hardware-based TEE; data remains encrypted in memory and is not readable by the hypervisor or Microsoft operators. DCasv5/v6 and DCsv3 verified available in UAE North on 2026-07-28. Customer Lockbox for Microsoft Azure Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/customer-lockbox-overview How: Gives the customer explicit approval rights over Microsoft engineer access to customer data during a support incident. Microsoft 'Defending Your Data' commitment Where: https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2020/11/19/defending-your-data-edpb-gdpr/ How: Public commitment to challenge government orders for customer data and to compensate affected customers. Microsoft Law Enforcement Requests Report Where: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/law-enforcement-requests-report How: Biannual transparency report of government requests, including rejections and challenges.
controls.reason: Exclusive UAE jurisdiction over consumer data cannot be asserted on commercial Azure because Microsoft Corporation remains subject to the US CLOUD Act. No Azure Policy can remediate a jurisdictional conflict. Must be escalated to legal and commercial negotiation; do not mark compliant.

controls.description: CSP shall ensure that all data, including consumer metadata, is not disclosed under any circumstances to any authority other than those explicitly approved by the UAE.

Microsoft publishes its record of government requests and its commitment to challenge orders, but cannot contractually guarantee non-disclosure against lawful US process. The durable mitigation is cryptographic: if Microsoft does not hold the key, it cannot produce readable data. Managed HSM external key management (preview) Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/external-key-management-overview How: Key encryption key stays in a customer-operated HSM outside Microsoft infrastructure. Gated: requires Microsoft account team enablement and USD 10M+ annual committed Azure spend. Azure Confidential Computing Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/overview How: Hardware-based TEE; data remains encrypted in memory and is not readable by the hypervisor or Microsoft operators. DCasv5/v6 and DCsv3 verified available in UAE North on 2026-07-28. Microsoft commitments on protection of customer data Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/protection-customer-data How: Covers Microsoft engineer access controls, just-in-time access and the position on government requests for customer data.
controls.reason: Non-disclosure to non-UAE authorities is constrained by the same US CLOUD Act exposure. Microsoft challenges requests and publishes transparency reporting, but the absolute requirement is not technically enforceable.

controls.description: All foreign access requests to data hosted within the cloud service shall be denied by default.

'Denied by default' cannot be attested by a certification body. Treat as a contractual clause plus the cryptographic controls in blocker B2. Managed HSM external key management (preview) Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/external-key-management-overview How: Key encryption key stays in a customer-operated HSM outside Microsoft infrastructure. Gated: requires Microsoft account team enablement and USD 10M+ annual committed Azure spend. Azure Confidential Computing Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/overview How: Hardware-based TEE; data remains encrypted in memory and is not readable by the hypervisor or Microsoft operators. DCasv5/v6 and DCsv3 verified available in UAE North on 2026-07-28. Customer Lockbox for Microsoft Azure Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/customer-lockbox-overview How: Gives the customer explicit approval rights over Microsoft engineer access to customer data during a support incident. Microsoft Law Enforcement Requests Report Where: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/law-enforcement-requests-report How: Biannual transparency report of government requests, including rejections and challenges.
controls.reason: Default denial of foreign access requests is a legal posture, not an Azure resource configuration.

controls.description: Policies for cryptography, encryption, and key management, shall be developed and implemented to ensure that data at rest and in transit is securely encrypted in compliance with the National Encryption Policy.
controls.reason: Microsoft maintains enterprise cryptographic policy and key-management standards. Data in transit is protected with TLS 1.2 or above, and data at rest is encrypted by default with FIPS 140 validated cryptographic modules. Customer-managed and customer-held key options are available through Azure Key Vault and Managed HSM. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 8.24 (use of cryptography); SOC 2 Type II criteria CC6.1 and CC6.7; FIPS 140-3 validation via the NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program. Microsoft control references DS-1 to DS-4, SC-8, SC-13, SC-28. EVIDENCE: 1. Microsoft Service Assurance - Encryption and key management: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-encryption 2. Azure ISO/IEC 27001 certificate and Statement of Applicability: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC 3. NIST CMVP validated modules list: https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program 4. SOC 2 Type II report (NDA required): https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC

controls.description: CSP shall offer mechanisms for Cloud Consumers to encrypt their data at rest and in transit, using strong, industry-accepted cryptographic algorithms and protocols. For data in transit between CSP environments, encryption shall be enforced by default.
controls.how_to_meet: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled ; Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version ; Transparent Data Encryption on SQL databases should be enabled
controls.reason: Encryption mechanisms for data at rest and in transit are directly evaluable across the storage and database estate: secure transfer and minimum TLS version cover transit; Transparent Data Encryption covers SQL at rest.
defender_recommendations: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
Transparent Data Encryption on SQL databases should be enabled

controls.description: CSP shall offer a practical and well-documented process for seamless integration and management of consumer-provided keys, enabling programmatic control over key generation, storage, retrieval, and rotation.
controls.how_to_meet: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled ; Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled ; Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption ; SQL servers should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
controls.reason: Bring Your Own Key integration is evidenced by customer-managed key usage on the data services plus the vault protections that prevent key destruction. The key ceremony and custody process itself remains manual.

controls.description: CSP shall support Hold Your Own Key (HYOK) capabilities, enabling cloud consumers to retain full control over their encryption keys by allowing them to generate, manage, and store cryptographic keys within their own trusted environments (e.g. on-premises or customer-controlled Hardware Security Modules).
controls.how_to_meet: OS and data disks should be encrypted with a customer-managed key ; Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption
controls.reason: Hold Your Own Key support requires single-tenant HSM-backed key storage. There is no built-in policy that mandates Managed HSM, so this is enforced by the custom definition 'eand-ncsp-managed-hsm-required' in the SLZ plane, supported by the built-in customer-managed key policies that force keys to resolve from that vault.

controls.description: CSP shall ensure that all hosted encryption keys, including their backups, are generated stored, and managed within the UAE to maintain full control over data security and sovereignty.
controls.how_to_meet: Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption ; SQL servers should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest ; Allowed locations
controls.reason: Keys hosted and managed within the UAE are enforced by combining customer-managed key requirements with the location allow-list, so the Key Vault or Managed HSM holding the key can only exist in a UAE region.

controls.description: CSP shall use UAE based Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) for the storage and protection of encryption keys.
controls.how_to_meet: No Azure Policy - Microsoft-attested control ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 clause 8.24 (use of cryptography); FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validation via NIST CMVP; Managed HSM regional data-residency commitment Azure Key Vault Managed HSM is available in UAE North and UAE Central (verified 2026-07-28 via 'az provider show -n Microsoft.KeyVault --query resourceTypes[?resourceType==managedHSMs].locations'). It is FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated, single-tenant, and Microsoft documents that it does not store or process customer data outside the deployment region. The customer holds the security domain, so Microsoft cannot access the keys. Residual: Microsoft does not publish a per-rack physical-location attestation for the HSM appliance. Evidence is the regional data-residency commitment plus the CMVP certificate, not a UAE site attestation. Azure Key Vault Managed HSM Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/overview How: FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated, single-tenant, customer-held security domain. Verified available in UAE North and UAE Central on 2026-07-28 via 'az provider show -n Microsoft.KeyVault'. NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program Where: https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program How: Search the CMVP validated-modules list for the Marvell LiquidSecurity adapter used by Managed HSM to obtain the FIPS 140-3 certificate. Managed HSM external key management (preview) Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/external-key-management-overview How: Key encryption key stays in a customer-operated HSM outside Microsoft infrastructure. Gated: requires Microsoft account team enablement and USD 10M+ annual committed Azure spend. Azure data residency and global infrastructure Where: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure/data-residency/ How: Authoritative per-service statement of where customer data is stored.
controls.reason: UAE-based hardware security modules for key storage are not offered as a customer-verifiable property of Azure Managed HSM in the UAE regions today. Azure Policy can require Managed HSM but cannot attest to the physical location and certification of the HSM estate. Escalate to Microsoft for written attestation.

controls.description: Cloud service shall ensure that all Consumer Data are stored strictly within the geographical boundaries and legal jurisdiction of the UAE.
controls.how_to_meet: Allowed locations ; Allowed locations for resource groups
controls.reason: Storage of consumer data within UAE boundaries is enforced at deploy time by the location allow-list applied at both resource and resource-group scope, evaluated before creation.

controls.description: CSP shall maintain an updated list of native services that can be consumed in compliance with the Partial Sovereign Cloud Requirements*. Additionally, any changes to the compliance status of the cloud services shall be communicated to the cloud consumer.
controls.how_to_meet: No Azure Policy - Microsoft-attested control ATTESTED BY: Not a certification item - satisfied by the published Azure data-residency and regional service-availability documentation Microsoft publishes per-service regional availability and data-residency positions. the Customer must maintain the derived Partial Sovereign service catalogue and re-validate it each release, because Microsoft changes regional availability without customer notice. Azure data residency and global infrastructure Where: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure/data-residency/ How: Authoritative per-service statement of where customer data is stored. Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty Where: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/industry/sovereignty/ How: Sovereign Landing Zone, sovereignty policy baseline and transparency controls.
controls.reason: Maintaining a current list of partial-sovereign compliant services is a Microsoft publication obligation, delivered through Azure product availability by region documentation.

controls.description: Location of the processing, storage, transfer, and backup of data shall be clearly communicated to the consumer and compliance with applicable contractual obligations, laws, and regulations in the UAE regarding data location and sovereignty shall be maintained at all stages.
controls.reason: Microsoft publishes, per service, where customer data is stored and processed, and commits contractually to the data-residency position in the Data Protection Addendum and Product Terms. Regional storage commitments are within the audited ISMS scope. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and Statement of Applicability; ISO/IEC 27018:2019 (transparency over PII processing locations). GAP: customer data residency is documented and committed, but some Azure control-plane metadata is processed globally and is not customer-configurable. Disclose this rather than claiming unqualified compliance. EVIDENCE: 1. Azure data residency and global infrastructure (per-service statement): https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure/data-residency/ 2. Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum: https://aka.ms/dpa 3. Azure ISO/IEC 27018 certificate: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC

controls.description: All metadata storage and processing activities shall be conducted strictly within the geographical boundaries and legal jurisdiction of the UAE.
controls.how_to_meet: No Azure Policy - Microsoft-attested control ATTESTED BY: PARTIALLY ATTESTABLE - customer data residency is documented; control-plane metadata residency is not customer-configurable Customer data stays in-region, and that is documented. controls.reason: Metadata residency is not customer-configurable. Certain Azure control-plane metadata is stored outside the geography by design; Microsoft documents this in the Azure data residency documentation. Escalate for written confirmation against the sovereign tier requirement.

controls.description: CSP shall maintain an updated list of native services that can be consumed in compliance with the Sovereign Cloud Requirements*. Additionally, any changes to the compliance status of the cloud services shall be communicated to the cloud consumer.

controls.description: CSP shall ensure the freedom of its cloud consumers to select their preferred provider for related services, allowing interoperability across cloud consumers and CSP environments and across different CSPs.

controls.reason: Freedom to select a preferred cloud provider is a commercial and contractual right, not an Azure resource configuration.

controls.how_to_meet: Azure/Entra configuration control
controls.reason: Open and published APIs for interoperability are a platform capability. Azure Resource Manager, Microsoft Graph and the Azure REST APIs are openly published, but no Azure Policy definition evaluates API openness.

controls.description: CSP shall enable portability using defined policies, standards or documented formats to ensure that cloud consumers are able to get their data into or out of cloud services in a reasonably easy and cost-effective manner.
controls.reason: Microsoft supports data portability through documented open formats and export tooling across Azure services, and commits in the Data Protection Addendum to enable retrieval of customer data during the term and for a defined retention window after termination. ATTESTED BY: ISO/IEC 27017:2015 (cloud-specific controls, including cloud-service customer data handling and return); the Data Protection Addendum data-retrieval provisions. EVIDENCE: 1. Azure ISO/IEC 27017 certificate: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC 2. Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum, data retention and deletion on termination: https://aka.ms/dpa 3. Per-service export and migration documentation on Microsoft Learn

controls.description: CSP shall use secure, standardized network protocols to import and export data and manage the service.
controls.how_to_meet: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled ; App Service apps should only be accessible over HTTPS ; Function apps should only be accessible over HTTPS ; Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version
controls.reason: Secure standardised network protocols are evaluable per service: HTTPS-only for App Service and Function Apps, secure transfer for storage, and a minimum TLS version floor.
defender_recommendations: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled

controls.description: CSP shall follow any policies and procedures defined by consumers in line with consumer's portability requirements.
controls.reason: NOT ATTESTABLE as written - Microsoft operates to its own published portability standards and does not undertake to follow customer-defined portability procedures. No ISO or SOC attestation covers conformance to a consumer's bespoke process. Treat as a contractual item: agree the portability procedure with Microsoft in the executed agreement, or accept Microsoft's published export capabilities as the delivery mechanism and hold the procedure on the the Customer side. Data Protection Addendum: https://aka.ms/dpa 3. the Customer-side portability procedure document (held by the Customer)

controls.description: CSP shall offer comprehensive documentation on data and workload portability mechanisms, emphasizing the consumer's ability to move their assets freely avoiding vendor lock-in.

Azure ISO/IEC 27017 certificate: https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/ISOIEC the Customer should cite the specific documentation pages for the services in its own service catalogue.

controls.description: Changes to the CSP's cloud infrastructure shall be preemptively planned and coordinated efficiently, ensuring compliance with applicable uptime requirements.

Changes to production infrastructure are planned, reviewed, tested and approved before deployment, with staged rollout and automated rollback to protect availability commitments. Microsoft Service Assurance - Governance and control frameworks: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-governance 2. Azure infrastructure integrity and operations: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/infrastructure-operations 3. SOC 2 Type II report (NDA required): https://servicetrust.microsoft.com/viewpage/SOC
